scenes.title: 블루프린트 작업 화면
lines: This is Epic’s Blueprint editor in action. A developer connects nodes and runs the game. An item appears beside the character, and the screen shows three collectibles left. This familiar way of making games in Unreal now has a planned end point. Two announcements tell us what changes, and when.

scenes.title: 6월 시카고 로드맵
lines: First, Chicago in June. Epic set out plans to bring its new language Verse to UE6 and make code easier to share between projects. At that point, developers would still be able to use Actors and Blueprints in the first versions of UE6. In November, the plan changed in Tokyo.

scenes.title: 11월 도쿄 발표
lines: According to Game Makers’ November 3 report from Tokyo, Epic plans to remove three systems from the first early-access release of UE6: Actors, Blueprints and the C++ gameplay framework. Here, C++ refers to the framework used to program gameplay. The engine still uses C++ for rendering and physics. Epic’s target for early access is the end of 2027.

scenes.title: 포트나이트의 전환
lines: An early look at the replacement is already available in Unreal Editor for Fortnite. Scene Graph organizes objects in the game world and their relationships. Developers write those objects’ behavior in Verse. Epic says it is migrating Fortnite itself to this architecture. It also plans to use AI to help migrate existing code.

scenes.title: 시카고 에디터 시연
lines: The Chicago demonstration shows what AI can already do in the editor. A rug and furniture appear in a previously empty room. The tool uses a protocol called MCP to place those objects in the Unreal Editor. This demo ran on Unreal Engine 5.8. In Tokyo, Epic said productivity on some internal tasks had increased by a factor of 1.5 to 4.

scenes.title: 언리얼을 계속 쓰는 이유
lines: With Blueprints set to change, why would a studio stick with Unreal? For a team with characters and levels already built in UE5, shipping the current game preserves that investment. In its November 3 announcement, Epic said it planned to release the UE5.9 preview the following week. A new team faces a different cost of switching.

scenes.title: 고도와 유니티의 조건
lines: Godot’s terms are straightforward. Godot publishes its source under the MIT license. Even commercial games pay no engine fee or revenue royalty. Distributions must include the engine’s copyright and license notice. Unity lets teams reuse their C# code and existing assets. For a studio making its own game, Unity Personal is free when revenue plus funding over the past 12 months is at most $200,000. Above that threshold, a US Unity Pro seat costs $2,310 per year when prepaid.

scenes.title: 출시 뒤 엔진 비용
lines: Unreal’s current standard game license uses a different measure: sales. If a Steam-only title grosses $1.2 million in its first quarter, the 5 percent rate on the $200,000 above the first million produces a $10,000 royalty to Epic. Godot charges no engine royalty, while Unity Pro is priced by seat. Epic’s announcement changes the case for choosing Unreal. For an established studio, the work invested in UE5 matters. For a new studio, the tools and the cost after launch can decide the choice.
